// era.ts.txt — SCANNED, NEVER RUN. The half of the era table that is not on
// the ecmascript timeline at all: TypeScript syntax reaches an environment
// through `env_extra` rather than through a year, and this file is what makes
// that path carry real sites instead of a claim.
//
// THE DECORATOR IS HERE SINCE 2026-09-08, and the paragraph it replaces is
// worth quoting because it was true and is not: "its absence is a fact about
// the SCANNER rather than about this fixture ... `@logged` is a hard parse
// ERROR — not a missing node, a refused file". That was recorded as
// `feature_unscannable(decorators, a_parser_plugin_not_enabled)` so a permanent
// absence would not read as a corpus gap. The owner asked for decorators, the
// scanner gained the plugin, and the waiver became a claim about a
// configuration that no longer exists — so it went, and this file owes the era
// table a real site for `decorators` instead.
//
// BOTH KINDS THE PLUGIN UNLOCKS ARE HERE, because they need SEPARATE plugins
// and one does not imply the other: `@logged` needs `decorators` and
// `accessor` needs `decoratorAutoAccessors`.
export function widen(n: number, s: string): number {
  const cast = (n as number) + 1;
  const shouted: string = s!;
  return cast + shouted.length;
}

export class Service {
  run(): string { return 'ran'; }
}

function logged(value, _ctx) { return value; }

@logged
export class Decorated {
  @logged run(): string { return 'ran'; }
  accessor slot = 1;
}
